title: Tasers save lives: coroner: Tells inquest more Ontario police forces should have Tasers
article: Tasers are safe and should be used even more frequently by Ontario police, a provincial coroner has told the inquest into a London man's death.

Since 2003, nine Canadians have died shortly after being shot by a police Taser, but Dr. Jim Cairns said Tuesday that experts nationwide agree the powerful stun guns didn't cause any deaths -- including the May 2004 death of Peter Lamonday.
"The evidence is overwhelming that (Tasers have) saved many, many lives," Cairns told the three-man, two-woman jury. "Taser me before you shoot me -- I'll take that."
"None of the deaths in Canada can be attributed to the Taser being used."

All nine people, Lamonday included, were determined to have died from the same cause: cocaine-induced excited delirium, which allows the rampaging person to feel no pain and exhibit superhuman strength before crashing.
The number of Canadians who survived being Tasered while experiencing excited delirium is unknown, Cairns said.
A Taser shoots 50,000 volts of electricity, temporarily paralysing the target. Though Tasers face much criticism, they've never been proved deadly.
Lamonday's rampage on May 13, 2004, ended with eight police officers struggling to arrest him. They finally handcuffed him following three Taser shots.
Lamonday was taken to London Health Sciences Centre and strapped, face down and still cuffed, on a stretcher. Within an hour, he was pronounced dead.

Cairns wrote a memo 10 years ago warning colleagues that keeping people experiencing excited delirium in that "prone position" could be deadly. It could have contributed to Lamonday's death, he said Tuesday.
"If he's in the prone position and there is pressure on his back, I would consider that to be a (possible factor)," he said.

As the provincial government's main Taser expert, Cairns also told the jury much of the negative media coverage of the powerful stun guns is "unsubstantiated when you look at the scientific evidence."
Cathy Colborne, Lamonday's widow, is expected to testify at the inquest today.
